title: I Forwarded the E-Scooter Geofence Ping After They Dumped It in My Vestibule

parts.text: I opened my vestibule at 7:41 a.m. and a lime scooter was wedged against the mailboxes outside the geofence hatch. The app photo on the stem said: END IN THE HATCH. NO LOBBIES. Rider name on the last ping was a vendor account. I was thirty-six, tenant, holding a blocked door. I photographed the stem, the hatch map, and the mailbox scrape. Then I forwarded the ping to the operator. At 7:49 the operator asked why a vendor account had ended in a vestibule. I did not argue the joke. I argued the file. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The operator can see a vendor-ended scooter against mailboxes outside the hatch.

social.video_title: They ended a vendor scooter in my vestibule — Part 1/2
social.description: E-scooter, a blocked door, and a hatch map on the stem. I forwarded the ping. Would you have photographed the scrape?

parts.text: The vendor called it a dead battery until the operator asked for the stills. I printed the ping, the photo, and the map. The scooter moved to the hatch. They ended in hatches and told riders batteries were always about optics. Optics is a word vendors use when a scrape exists. Geofence now has a second line: VESTIBULES ARE NOT HATCHES. I keep a clear door. They hatch. The lobby finally looks like mail, not a dock. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Ping stills, moved scooter, and a second line. Was a dead battery ever my mailboxes?
